steps: Triangles ABD and ADC share the height from A to BC, so their areas are in the ratio 3:1.
E is the midpoint of AC, so area ADE is half of area ADC. Therefore area ABD : area ADE = 6:1.
ABD and ADE share base AD. Their perpendicular heights from B and E to AD are consequently in the ratio 6:1.
B, P and E lie on one straight line, with P on AD. Their heights to AD scale with distance from P (similar right triangles), giving BP:PE = 6:1.
Area ABE is half of ABC, or 28 cm². ABP and APE share the height from A to BE, so ABP takes 6/7 of ABE.
